shortDescription: Shares of Chinese chipmakers Hosin Electronics (2681.HK) and Amicro Technology (2065.HK) rose in their Hong Kong debut on Thursday after the companies raised a combined HK$1.78 billion ($227 million) in initial public offerings.($1 = 7.8459 Hong Kong dollars)

children: Shares of Chinese chipmakers Hosin Electronics (2681.HK) and Amicro Technology (2065.HK) rose in their Hong Kong debut on Thursday after the companies raised a combined HK$1.78 billion ($227 million) in initial public offerings.
Hosin opened at HK$72.80, down 0.04% from its offer price of HK$72.83, and last traded at HK$72.90. Amicro opened at HK$13.62, up 37.6% from its HK$9.90 offer price, and last traded at HK$16.81
slipped 1.1%, while the Hang Seng Tech Index
Hosin raised HK$1.07 billion by selling 14.72 million shares at HK$72.83 each. The Hong Kong retail tranche was 2.37 times subscribed and the international offering 1.45 times covered

Hosin, a developer of memory products including embedded storage, solid-state drives, DRAM and portable storage devices, plans to use most of the proceeds to develop memory products and controller chips and expand testing capabilities, with the remainder earmarked for working capital and general corporate purposes
Amicro raised HK$709.7 million by selling 71.69 million shares at HK$9.90 apiece. Its Hong Kong retail offering was 13.95 times subscribed, while the international tranche was 1.05 times covered

Amicro, which develops intelligent mobile robotics solutions, will use most proceeds to manufacture software, hardware and AI chips for robots, with the rest allotted to help expand sales, investments and its working capital

title: Chinese chip firms Hosin, Amicro rise in Hong Kong debuts
